entries.verbatim: Taking this up commits the household to a few concrete behaviours, not to agreeing with my diagnosis. Maintaining a single shared written record after each agreement, plus explicit definitions of done for recurring tasks — that is the load-bearing part, and it only works if all three treat it as a memory aid rather than a dossier; the record itself can become ammunition if used to score points, which is a real risk I flag rather than solve. Setting and protecting a short weekly check-in, and the inviter specifically shortening conversations after asking the avoiding friend what would help — the advice about avoidance depends on that follow-through. Tolerating approximate fairness is a scope choice, not a finding; if the underlying grievance is about respect or money rather than tasks, this system will paper over it and my recommendations should be revised. The one-month trial is a proposed test, and I am proposing it fallibly: persistent avoidance or escalation despite the structure would count against my claim that this is mainly a coordination problem, not confirm it. If one flatmate refuses even the trial, only the unilateral parts remain available to the asker — confirming agreements in writing, stating their own standards, attending to tone — and I cannot claim those alone resolve a three-person dispute. Unresolved: what to do when the avoiding friend also avoids the meta-conversation, which this account does not cover.

entries.verbatim: Taking this up involves treating three conjectures as live but unproven: that the reinterpretation disputes are underspecification failures rather than bad faith; that changing schedules make any one-time fair split decay, so a renegotiation rhythm matters more than the initial split; and that the friend's avoidance tracks the felt cost of the conversations. The proposed applications are the written agreement log, the time-boxed check-in, the pre-agreed remedy for missed chores, and the separate low-stakes talk with the avoidant friend. Cheap tests are attached: two to four weeks of written agreements should end the 'that is not what we agreed' disputes if the memory conjecture is right; if they persist in writing, drop that conjecture and redirect toward explicit done-criteria or a renegotiated fairness of the split. If the friend will not attend even a fifteen-minute time-boxed check-in, the procedural reading of his avoidance fails and the problem is likely relational, needing a different kind of conversation entirely. Criticisms I accept in advance: the account rests entirely on one party's report, so the narrator's own contribution to the dynamic goes unexamined; coordination tools do not address standards-mismatch, money, or friendship-level resentment if those are what actually carries the conflict; and the check-in system itself can become one more obligation people shirk. Unresolved: nothing in the exposed material says who is right in any current dispute, and I am not proposing to adjudicate that.

entries.verbatim: Taking up this objection means treating four criticisms as live but unproven. (1) The claimed tension between a conversation-cost diagnosis and a conversation-heavy remedy commits me to the existence and feasibility of lower-conversation architectures such as standing domain ownership; it loses force if per-instance negotiation is failing only at the level of wording rather than as a mechanism, and I concede the ownership alternative inherits the account's own bootstrapping problem since it too requires an initial negotiation the avoider may refuse. (2) The motivated-interpretation and asymmetric-tolerance rival is a conjecture resting on facts not exposed in the problem text; a cheap discriminator is available — disputes over the meaning of specific written items support the rival, while disputes about whether anything was agreed support the memory conjecture — and my sequencing criticism, if applied by moving the separate low-stakes talk first, would itself produce evidence for or against the rival. (3) The confounding criticism of the attendance test commits me to claiming the account's tests are weakly identifying until schedule constraints are ruled out, not to claiming its conjectures are false. (4) The sequencing and administration-cost claims depend on the narrator's actual role in the flat dynamic and on who would run the proposed system; these cannot be verified from the exposed material, so adopting them means asking rather than asserting. Criticisms I accept in advance: the account already hedges its program and disclaims adjudicating current disputes, so part of my pressure lands on language it qualified; my strategic-behavior framing may overweight calculation against temperament, fatigue, or low mood as causes of avoidance; and nothing here settles whether an alternative architecture fits the flat's money constraints or standards gap, or which flatmate, if any, is in the right.
